reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Scoring the spot sign (CTA) here; BAT uses non-contrast CT only.
name: BAT Score for Haematoma Expansion

version.label: BAT score (Morotti et al. 2018)
version.detail: Blend sign 1, any intrahaematoma hypodensity 2, time from onset to CT under 2.5 hours 2; total 0–5. A score of 3 or more identified higher risk of expansion.

purpose: Estimates the risk of haematoma expansion from non-contrast CT and timing.
intendedPopulation: Adults with spontaneous ICH imaged early with non-contrast CT; patients with coagulopathy were excluded from derivation.

inputDefinitions.label: Blend sign
inputDefinitions.help: Hypodense and hyperdense regions with a well-defined margin, visible density difference of at least 18 HU.

inputDefinitions.label: Time from onset to CT under 2.5 hours

resultStates.label: BAT {total}
resultStates.detail: Expansion can still occur; repeat imaging depends on the clinical course.

resultStates.label: Higher expansion risk (≥3)
resultStates.summary: BAT 3 or more: higher risk of haematoma expansion in the derivation and validation cohorts.
resultStates.detail: Assess and monitor according to the clinical situation and local protocol.

clinicalContext.text: Combines two non-contrast CT signs with early presentation to identify likely haematoma expansion.

clinicalInsights.text: Expansion is a modifiable determinant of outcome; time from onset matters.

limitations: CT sign interpretation varies between readers.
whatItDoesNotTellYou: Whether a specific treatment will reduce expansion.

guideSections.what: Blend sign (1) + any hypodensity (2) + CT within 2.5 h of onset (2), total 0–5.
guideSections.whenToUse: Early non-contrast CT in spontaneous ICH.
guideSections.howToPerform: Look for a blend sign and intrahaematoma hypodensities; note time from onset to CT; sum.
guideSections.clinicalContext: An expansion risk marker alongside volume and clinical status.

sources.citation: Morotti A, Dowlatshahi D, Boulouis G, et al. Predicting intracerebral hemorrhage expansion with noncontrast computed tomography: the BAT score. Stroke. 2018;49(5):1163-1169.

components.label: Time from onset to CT under 2.5 hours
